standing: OURS: a labelled decision record for the bounded, offline, review-only A05 assembly experiment Christian authorized in his second reply of 5 November 2026. It is not a knowledge file, not a configuration step (the architecture has none: Steps 3-5 are held), not served, and not an authorization. Every value states how it reached the activity and which of his six classes it falls in; values his words do not state are ILLUSTRATIVE, OURS or UNRESOLVED. Nothing on the live route or the checked pathway reads this file.

requirements.statement: The choice between the related Game Problems must depend on the interaction circumstances. A primary or secondary designation made for one execution is not a permanent hierarchy between them.
words: Create Space and Exploit Space should not have a permanent hierarchical relationship simply because one is designated primary in this particular execution.
When an organized defense is meaningfully restricting available space, creating additional opportunities may be the dominant problem.
When useful space is already available, exploiting it may be the immediate problem. Players shouldn't be encouraged to create space unnecessarily.
The selected Game Problem should ultimately depend on the interaction circumstances, not simply the wording of the Learning Goal.
requirements.whatIsMissing: No loaded knowledge relates interaction circumstances (how far an organized defense restricts space, whether useful space is already available) to the choice between these Game Problems, and the stage receives no description of those circumstances. Stage 1 therefore uses the scoped designation and reports this requirement as open on every resolution it applies to.

sentences.text: Improve attacking conditions while maintaining purposeful possession.
The game is played by 2 teams against each other: each team attacks the target zone at one end and defends the target zone at the other end.
Area: 40 x 30 m, including both target zones; there are no goalkeepers, so none are counted.
Players: 6 v 6, equal numbers.
Duration: 3 blocks of 6 minutes, with a short break between blocks.
Each team scores a point when one of its players gets the ball under control in the target zone it attacks; there is no offside.
Diagram: not drawn here; in this review the diagram depends on the checked activity pathway, which draws a diagram from a realized game.
Mark out a 40 x 30 m area with a halfway line and a centre mark.
At each end, mark a target zone 5 m deep across the full width of the area; both target zones are inside the area.
The exact position of the target zones is not yet decided; this example puts them at the ends of the area.
Divide the players into 2 teams of 6; give each team its own bib colour and keep it for the whole session.
Equipment: markers for the area, the halfway line, the centre mark and both target zones, and spare balls.
Each team attacks one target zone and defends the other for the whole game.
Both teams attack and defend, and both score in the same way, in the target zone each attacks.
Play continues when the ball changes teams; a change of possession does not stop play.
There is no offside.
Any player may enter either target zone at any time.
Fouls are penalized with free kicks, as in the normal Laws.
No player may handle the ball: there are no goalkeepers.
The normal Laws of the game apply to everything not described here.

A team scores a point with a controlled arrival in the target zone it attacks, as the approved scoring event describes it: "A player dribbles into a marked zone, or receives and controls the ball inside it."
A controlled arrival in the target zone counts even straight after the team has won the ball.
The role of the attack's starting condition in scoring is not yet decided; in this example it does not change whether an arrival in the target zone counts.
The team with more points at the end of a block wins that block.
Nothing changes between blocks: each team keeps its bib colour, the target zone it attacks and its direction.
Start with an ordinary kick-off from the centre mark.
The kick-off follows the normal Laws.
After a point, the team that conceded it restarts play with a kick-off.
When the ball goes over a touchline, the team that did not touch it last restarts with a throw-in.
When the ball goes over an end line, the team that did not touch it last restarts play from the end line where it went out.
With no goals, the normal Laws give no restart for a ball over an end line, so the restart above is this example's own.
There are no goals, so there are no penalty kicks, goal kicks or corner kicks.
No adjustments are offered in this example.
These categories describe how a score came about, for reviewing this example; there is no target for any of them.
Against organized opposition: The team progresses and scores after confronting a defense that has established or recovered its organization.
During transition: The team scores before the opposition has recovered its organization.
Uncertain: The coach cannot confidently distinguish the situation.
Both scoring situations remain legitimate.
The categories do not decide whether an arrival in the target zone counts, and they do not settle the role of the attack's starting condition, which stays an open part of scoring.
